title: Marked coordinate divisor parameters under etale pullback
statement: Let $C$ be a commutative Noetherian regular ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-regular-scheme], $U=\operatorname{Spec}C$, and $z_1,\ldots,z_r\in C$, with $r\ge0$. Suppose that at each $y\in U$ the vanishing members of this indexed list occupy distinct positions in a regular system of parameters of $\mathcal O_{U,y}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Put $P=\prod_{j=1}^r z_j$, with empty product $1$, and $D=V(P)$. For every etale morphism $h:W\to U$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], including $h=1_U$, the scheme $W$ is regular and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. More precisely, for each $w\in W$, $y=h(w)$, the stalk map takes every chosen full regular system of parameters of $\mathcal O_{U,y}$ to a full regular system of parameters of $\mathcal O_{W,w}$. The pullback germ $z_j(w)$ is a nonunit exactly when $z_j(y)$ is a nonunit, and these vanishing germs occupy the same distinct parameter positions. The local equation $h^*P$ is a unit times the product of precisely those marked parameter germs. Multiplication by $P$ on $C$, and multiplication by $h^*P$ on every local ring of $W$, are injective. Consequently $h^{-1}D$ is an effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] with normal crossings [def-trf-normal-crossings-divisor], allowing the empty divisor. Its number of geometric branches at a geometric point above $w$ equals $\#\{j:z_j(y)\in\mathfrak m_y\}\le r$, independently of the etale neighborhood. Using strict henselizations [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization], a geometric branch means a minimal prime of the reduced strict henselian local ring of the divisor, with number zero off the divisor. If $r=0$, then $P=1$ and all these divisors are empty.

proof.text: By [def-weil-regular-scheme] and [pqf-def-locnoeth], $U=\operatorname{Spec}C$ is regular and locally Noetherian. Apply [lem-trf-etale-coordinate-intersection-geometry] to the list $z_1,\ldots,z_r,1$ of length $r+1\geq1$ and to $h$. The appended unit vanishes nowhere, so this list satisfies exactly the given condition on distinct parameter positions. The cited statement gives regularity and local Noetherianity of $W$, transport of every chosen full regular system from $\mathcal O_{U,y}$ to $\mathcal O_{W,w}$, and equality of the vanishing index sets. In a local ring the elements with zero residue are precisely its nonunits. Thus, writing $I_y=\{j:z_j(y)\in\mathfrak m_y\}$, the pullbacks indexed by $I_y$ occupy the same distinct positions in the transported system; precisely the remaining germs are units.

In $R=\mathcal O_{W,w}$ put $x_j=h^*z_j$ for $j\in I_y$ and $v=\prod_{j\notin I_y}h^*z_j$. Every factor of $v$ is a unit by Step 1, so $v$ is a unit, and the ring-homomorphism and finite-product identities give $h^*P=v\prod_{j\in I_y}x_j$. This proves the asserted local equation, including $I_y=\varnothing$, when the equation is a unit. The indexed sublist has no repeated parameter position by Step 1.

The full system in $R$ generates its maximal ideal and has length $\dim R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], every permutation is an $R$-regular sequence. For each marked $x_j$, choose a permutation putting that parameter first. By [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], multiplication by this first parameter on $R$ is injective. Multiplication by $\prod_{j\in I_y}x_j$ is the composite of these injective multiplication maps and hence is injective; for the empty product it is the identity. Multiplication by the unit $v$ is invertible, so multiplication by $h^*P$ is injective on $R$. This applies to every $w$ and also to $h=1_U$.

source.place: Tag 00NQ, lemma-regular-ring-CM, applied after permuting the regular system; definition of a regular sequence

proof.text: Local injectivity implies injectivity on affine sections by the following explicit argument. For an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset W$, write $f=(h^*P)|_V\in B$ and suppose $fb=0$. Step 3 implies $b/1=0$ in $B_{\mathfrak p}$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$. If $b\neq0$, its annihilator is a proper ideal; choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$ containing it. The equality $b/1=0$ gives an $s\notin\mathfrak p$ with $sb=0$, contrary to $s\in\operatorname{Ann}(b)\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Thus $b=0$. Applying the same argument to $\operatorname{Spec}C$ with $h=1_U$ proves injectivity of multiplication by $P$ on $C$. In the zero ring injectivity holds directly.

source.place: Elementary annihilator and localization argument supplementing Tags 00NQ and 00KU

proof.text: The inverse image closed subscheme $h^{-1}D=D\times_UW$ has on each affine $V$ the principal ideal $(f)$: pulling back a principal equation replaces $P$ by $h^*P$. Step 4 proves that this generator is a non-zero-divisor. Hence [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] makes this an effective Cartier divisor. At every $w$ its stalk ideal equals $(\prod_{j\in I_y}x_j)$ by Step 2, with distinct members of a full regular system. Taking the identity etale neighborhood of $W$ in [def-trf-normal-crossings-divisor] proves normal crossings, including the empty sublist. In particular this also proves the assertion about $D$ by taking $h=1_U$.

source.place: Expose VIII 4.1.2, printed p.117, local product-of-parameters description; 4.1.8, printed p.118

proof.text: Fix a geometric point over $w$ and let $H$ be a strict henselization of $R$ with the induced separable residue-field closure [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Apply [lem-trf-parameter-product-strict-local-branches] to $R$ and the distinct marked parameters $x_j$ from Step 1, and set $F=\prod_{j\in I_y}x_j$. For $I_y\neq\varnothing$ it says that $H/(F)$ is a strict henselization of $R/(F)$ and that its reduction has exactly $|I_y|$ minimal primes. The unit $v$ gives $(h^*P)=(F)$ both in $R$ and in $H$, so these quotients compute exactly the divisor in the statement. This proves the required geometric branch count. For $I_y=\varnothing$ the equation is a unit, the divisor is absent at $w$, and the branch count is zero; the cited lemma also treats $F=1$. Since $|I_y|$ is computed at $y$ and Step 1 preserves this same index set for every $h$ and $w$, the number is independent of the etale neighborhood and is at most $r$. If $r=0$ then $P=1$ globally and every divisor under discussion is empty.
